Corporate.scope:
Bridger Corporate Travel works across:
• Real-time spend visibility
• Policy compliance built in
• Traveler experience that doesn't generate complaints

Corporate.tagline: Travel management and booking technology for mid-market enterprises.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: Hartwell is a surname with a quiet establishment register. Travel Holdings signals the holding-company structure with multiple operating brands underneath. The pair reads as an institutional travel management group, not a consumer brand.
Corporate.manifesto: Hartwell Travel Holdings operates corporate travel management and a connected booking technology platform across mid-market enterprises. The buyer is a head of procurement or a CFO. The contract is the year. The metric is travel policy compliance, spend reduction, and traveler satisfaction.
Corporate.industrySummary: Corporate travel management has consolidated under a small number of global TMCs. The mid-market is under-served by both the global TMCs (too expensive, too slow) and the SMB tools (too thin). The opening is for a serious mid-market TMC with proprietary booking technology and policy enforcement.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: CWT (mycwt.com) is the global TMC reference. American Express GBT (amexglobalbusinesstravel.com) is the peer at the top. TripActions / Navan (navan.com) holds the tech-forward middle. We sit in the regional mid-market TMC category.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Hartwell Travel Holdings is a mid-market corporate travel management group with proprietary booking technology and full policy administration.
Corporate.positioningRationale: We compete on the combination of TMC service depth and modern booking technology. The CFO sees the spend reduction; the traveler sees a tool that works.

targetAudience.primary: Heads of procurement, CFOs, and travel managers at companies with $100M–$2B in revenue.
behaviors: Manage annual travel spend of $1M–$25M.
Negotiate corporate rates with hotel chains and airlines.
Report travel KPIs to the CFO quarterly.
Run RFPs for TMC services every three to five years.
motivations: Want a TMC with both service depth and modern booking tech.
Want measured spend reduction.
Want policy enforcement that travelers do not hate.

dos: Lead with spend metrics, compliance rates, and policy outcomes.
Speak the language of CFOs and travel managers.
Publish a quarterly mid-market corporate travel benchmark.
Reference actual customer titles in case studies.

messagingPillars.name: Service and technology
messagingPillars.description: Full TMC service — RFP support, contracted rates, account management — combined with a modern booking tool travelers actually use.

messagingPillars.name: Policy enforcement that works
messagingPillars.description: Policy rules are built into the booking flow. The traveler sees the in-policy options first; the out-of-policy options require a one-line reason.

messagingPillars.name: Spend reduction in writing
messagingPillars.description: Each engagement begins with a written savings target. The quarterly review shows actual against target by spend category.

Corporate.logoDirection: A serif wordmark — Hartwell set in a traditional book serif, with 'Travel Holdings' beneath in tracked small caps. Used in proposals, contracts, and on the office door. Not used on the consumer-facing booking tool.

typography.primary: A traditional book serif for the wordmark and proposals.
typography.secondary: A clean enterprise grotesque for reports, dashboards, and the booking tool.
typography.rationale: Tables and numbers tabular and disciplined.

Corporate.brandDescription: Bellweather Travel Holdings operates a portfolio of travel brands across leisure travel, tour operations, and travel-technology categories.
Corporate.scope:
Bellweather Travel Holdings works across:
• Multi-brand travel operations
• Shared distribution and reservation infrastructure
• Tour operations across multiple brands
• Travel-insurance and ancillary services
• Annual investor and operator reporting
Corporate.mission: To provide a serious operating platform for mid-tier travel brands that want to keep their identity and outsource the operations.
Corporate.vision: A travel operator whose portfolio brands grow under their own names because the distribution and operations are shared.
coreValues: Senior — partners deal with partners.
Operational — distribution runs on schedule.
Reliable — predictable operations across brands.
Discreet — brand relationships stay private.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: Bellweather is a real American place-name with a heritage trade register. Travel Holdings follows the multi-brand operator naming convention used in travel (TUI Group, Hotelplan, Trafalgar/TTC structure). The pair reads as an institutional operator with multi-brand portfolio scale.
Corporate.manifesto: Bellweather Travel Holdings owns and operates a portfolio of travel brands. Each brand retains its identity, leadership, and customer relationships; we operate the shared distribution, reservation infrastructure, and back office. The buyer is a brand founder considering sale, a distribution partner seeking single-vendor relationships, or an institutional investor holding travel assets.
Corporate.industrySummary: Travel has consolidated under a small number of multi-brand operators (TUI Group, Booking Holdings, Expedia Group). The opening underneath is for a regional mid-tier multi-brand operator.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: TUI Group (tuigroup.com) is the multi-brand travel reference. Hotelplan Group (hotelplan.com) holds the multi-brand peer slot. Trafalgar/TTC (ttc.com) sits in the multi-brand peer position. Audley Travel (audleytravel.com) plays the multi-region peer reference. We belong in the regional mid-tier multi-brand travel operator category.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Bellweather Travel Holdings is a regional multi-brand travel operator running shared distribution, reservation infrastructure, and tour operations across a portfolio of brands.
Corporate.positioningRationale: We compete on shared distribution depth, reservation-infrastructure scale, and operational reliability.

targetAudience.primary: Travel brand founders considering sale, distribution partners seeking single-vendor brand relationships, and institutional investors holding travel assets.
behaviors: Manage multi-brand travel operations.
Negotiate multi-year supplier and distribution agreements.
Care about reservation volume, supplier mix, and operating margin.
Renew on multi-year operating terms.
motivations: Need an operator with shared distribution.
Need to keep brand identity post-acquisition.
Need shared reservation infrastructure.

dos: Lead with brand portfolio, distribution footprint, and reservation volume.
Speak the language of brand founders, distribution partners, and procurement.
Publish quarterly operator letters.
Refer to brands by name, not by Bellweather tagging.
donts: No social media at the parent level.
No brand consolidation announcements without partner alignment.

messagingPillars.name: Multi-brand operator
messagingPillars.description: We own and operate four to eight travel brands across leisure, tour, and travel-tech categories. Each retains its identity.

messagingPillars.name: Shared distribution
messagingPillars.description: Centralized distribution and reservation infrastructure across the portfolio. Brands share booking systems and supplier relationships.

messagingPillars.name: Tour operations
messagingPillars.description: Shared tour operations across brands. Brands inherit operational scale through Bellweather's infrastructure.

Corporate.logoDirection: A serif wordmark — Bellweather set in a traditional book serif, with 'Travel Holdings' beneath in tracked small caps. Used in contracts and the corporate office. Not used on consumer-facing brands.

typography.primary: A traditional book serif for the wordmark and corporate letters.
typography.secondary: A clean enterprise grotesque for operational reports.

Creative.brandNameRationale: Single word. Names the goal of every traveler in one. Elsewhere is where the customer wants to be. The brand sits on that desire, plain and confident.
Creative.manifesto: Most travel brands sell the same five destinations on rotation. We sell the elsewhere. The trip the customer didn't know they wanted. The off-day in a place they hadn't thought to consider. The strange dinner. The wrong turn. The brand exists to send people somewhere else.
Creative.industrySummary: Travel brand has gotten cautious and beige. Linen-on-a-beach photography. The same lookbook for every destination. There's room for one that's loud, character-driven, sticker-friendly, and serious about finding the actual interesting places.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Atlas Obscura (atlasobscura.com) does the curiosity side well. Roam (joinroam.com) has the digital nomad community. Trover, before its closure, did some of this. We sit closer to Atlas Obscura with a sharper modern brand.
Creative.positioningStatement: A travel brand for people who pick the destination based on the rumor, not the brochure.

targetAudience.primary: 25 to 45. Travels often, alone or in twos. Reads the niche city blog over the major travel magazine. Eats at the place with no English menu. Tells friends about the trip and never about the brand.

dos: Tell the rumor
Name the strange place by its real name
Use real customer notes in the guide
donts: Curate a list of the top ten anything

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark in a punchy display serif, with the E of ELSEWHERE stylized as a small compass-rose section. Standalone compass-fragment icon for stickers, social profiles, and the back of every printed guide.

colorPalette.name: Elsewhere Orange
colorPalette.meaning: Sunset on a town you can't find on the map.
colorPalette.usage: Primary brand color, hero surfaces, totebags

colorPalette.name: Compass Blue
colorPalette.meaning: Anchor. The water on the map.

typography.primary: Migra for the wordmark and big display
typography.secondary: PP Neue Montreal for body and itineraries
typography.rationale: Migra has character and warmth. Neue Montreal keeps the practical details readable. The pair feels designed and curious.

customSections.title: What it isn't
customSections.body: Not a luxury travel brand. Not a list-of-ten-things brand. Not afraid of orange. Not too cool to tell you about the bus.

customSections.title: Where it lives
customSections.body: Printed guides for specific small cities. Totebags people actually use abroad. A monthly newsletter that's mostly customer notes. A pop-up travel office twice a year in a different city each time. Stickers in every order.

Creative.tagline: A travel brand for the scenic route.
Creative.brandNameRationale: The Long Way is a phrase travelers use to describe choosing the slower, more interesting route. As a brand name it stakes a position against efficiency tourism.
Creative.manifesto: Travel marketing sells the cathedral, the viewpoint, the rooftop bar. We started Not Today because the actual good day in a city is mostly the things the brochure left out. The neighborhood breakfast place, the bus to the suburb, the bookshop that closes at four. We make trips out of the rest of the city — the parts the camera tour does not stop at.
Creative.industrySummary: Travel content has become identical. Every blog, every video, every brand recommends the same dozen things per city. There is real space for a brand that builds trips around what the guidebooks left out.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Atlas Obscura (atlasobscura.com) plays the unusual-corner content slot. Culture Trip (theculturetrip.com) sits in the listicle middle. Wallpaper City Guides (wallpaper.com) is the design-led peer. We sit further out — a brand built around an opinion, not a list.
Creative.positioningStatement: Not Today is a trip-planning brand that builds itineraries around the city the guidebook left out.
Creative.positioningRationale: Every itinerary starts by removing the obvious sites. The brand stakes its credibility on the suburbs, the side streets, the closing-time bookshops.

targetAudience.primary: Travelers 28–50 who have already done the obvious and want the next layer.
behaviors: Skip the museum and find the café across from it.
Read the local newspaper before arriving.
Avoid named tourist neighborhoods.
Look up where locals eat on Tuesday.
motivations: Want a trip that feels like staying with a friend.
Want the city without the brochure.
Want a brand with an opinion.

dos: Tell the customer what to skip first.
Write itineraries in a city-friend voice.
Use neighborhood names, not landmark names.
Sign each itinerary by the planner's first name.
donts: No recommendations the customer has seen before.

messagingPillars.name: Skip list first
messagingPillars.description: Every itinerary opens with a skip list — the obvious sites we are not sending you to and why.

messagingPillars.name: Suburb day
messagingPillars.description: Every multi-day trip includes one full day outside the central district. The suburb day is often the best day.

messagingPillars.name: Local newspaper
messagingPillars.description: We send a short briefing of the local newspaper the week before the trip. What is opening, what is on, what is closed.

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark — The Long Way in a quiet display serif, with a small strike-through indicating refusal. The strike-through is the brand mark.

colorPalette.name: Stamp
colorPalette.meaning: Primary accent — the strike-through and the wordmark.

typography.secondary: A modern grotesque for itineraries and working type.
typography.rationale: The serif declares the opinion. The sans tells you what to do with it.

Creative.tagline: A travel brand for the people who pick the window seat.
Creative.brandDescription: The Window Seat Co is a creative-led travel brand specializing in train and ship travel — the slow modes where the window seat is the experience — with itineraries built entirely around scenic routes and journeys rather than destinations.
Creative.scope:
The Window Seat Co works across:
• Train and ship travel itineraries
• Scenic-route planning across continents
• Customer journals for documenting trips
• Quarterly published essays on slow travel
• Annual gathering of customers who travel by train and ship
Creative.mission: To make the journey the trip rather than the destination.
Creative.vision: A travel brand whose customers return year after year for the window seat.
coreValues: Warm — the journey is the trip.
Specific — the route is the experience.
Considered — every itinerary builds around the window seat.
Literary — the writing about slow travel is part of the brand.
Creative.brandNameRationale: The Window Seat is the universal traveler's phrase for the seat with a view — by train, plane, or ship. Naming the brand after the seat stakes a clear position around the journey as the central experience. The definite article + Co suffix follows the considered-creative trade-name school.
Creative.manifesto: Most travel optimizes for arrival speed. We started The Window Seat Co for the opposite — train journeys, ship crossings, scenic routes where the window seat is the experience. The journey is the trip; the destination is the pause.
Creative.industrySummary: Travel marketing optimizes around destinations. There is real space for a creative-led brand that positions on the journey itself.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Belmond (belmond.com) plays the heritage rail-and-cruise peer at premium. Off the Beaten Track Holidays plays the slow-travel peer slot. Great Rail Journeys (greatrail.com) holds the rail-focused peer position. Cunard (cunard.com) plays the heritage ocean peer reference. We sit alongside Great Rail Journeys with a sharper window-seat creative position.
Creative.positioningStatement: The Window Seat Co is a travel brand specializing in train and ship itineraries with the journey as the central experience.
Creative.positioningRationale: The brand competes on the journey premise. Every itinerary, every published essay, and every gathering is built around the window seat.

targetAudience.primary: Travelers 35-65 who prefer train and ship travel and care about the journey itself.
behaviors: Choose trains and ships over flights.
Plan trips around scenic routes.
Read travel writing about journeys.
Want unhurried itineraries.
motivations: Want a brand that prioritizes the journey.
Want scenic-route itineraries.
Want a community of slow travelers.

dos: Lead with the route and the journey.
Photograph the windows and the views.
Publish the quarterly essay on slow travel.
Sign correspondence by the planner.

messagingPillars.name: Train and ship only
messagingPillars.description: Every itinerary is built on train, ship, or both. We do not plan flights.

messagingPillars.name: Scenic routes
messagingPillars.description: Routes are selected for the window view. The journey is documented; the route is the marketing.

messagingPillars.name: Customer journals
messagingPillars.description: Customers receive a printed journal at the start of every trip for documenting the journey. The journals are part of the brand.

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark — The Window Seat Co set in a quiet display serif with a small illustration of a window frame beside it. The mark appears on customer journals and printed itineraries.

colorPalette.name: Sky
colorPalette.meaning: Primary — the colour of the view from the window.

typography.secondary: A book serif for the customer journals and printed itineraries.
typography.rationale: Two related serifs. The brand reads like a small printed travel publication.
